name: Steno's Laws of Stratigraphy
statement: Steno held that sedimentary layers form horizontally, extend continuously outward, and stack with the oldest at the bottom and youngest on top.
statementAccent: sedimentary layers form horizontally, extend continuously outward
meaning: These three principles — superposition, original horizontality, and lateral continuity — let geologists read the relative order of events from an undisturbed rock sequence without any absolute dating. Superposition establishes a bottom-to-top chronology; original horizontality assumes strata were laid flat before later tilting; lateral continuity assumes layers originally extended in all directions until thinning out or being cut off.
mechanism: Applied together, a geologist can infer which layers are older, reconstruct their original flat orientation even if now tilted or folded, and correlate matching layers across separated outcrops, treating any interruption as evidence of a later erosional or structural event.

examples.text: In an undeformed sequence, a shale bed lying beneath a sandstone bed is inferred to be older than the sandstone above it.
Tilted or folded strata in mountain ranges are interpreted as having originally been deposited flat and later deformed by tectonic forces.
A distinctive rock layer exposed on both sides of a river valley is inferred to have once been a single continuous bed before the valley eroded through it.

whyItMatters: Steno’s principles, published in 1669, founded the discipline of stratigraphy and gave geology its first systematic method for reconstructing relative geologic time, underpinning everything from oil and gas exploration to reading the fossil record.
limits: The laws assume relatively undisturbed deposition; they can be violated or complicated by overturned folds, igneous intrusions, unconformities, and localised environments where layers pinch out naturally rather than being cut by later events.
misreadings: Superposition is sometimes wrongly applied to deformed or overturned sequences without first checking for structural inversion, which can reverse the apparent age order.
origin: Formulated by Nicolas Steno (Niels Steensen), a Danish anatomist and later Catholic bishop, in his 1669 work "De solido intra solidum naturaliter contento dissertationis prodromus."

sources.text: Nicolas Steno, Wikipedia. — his 1669 Dissertationis prodromus and the principles of superposition, original horizontality, and lateral continuity.
Law of superposition, Wikipedia. — that Steno first proposed the principle in 1669 in Dissertationis prodromus.
